children.name: Melanocharis
children.description: The typical berrypeckers — a genus of small, fruit-eating passerines endemic to New Guinea, with short tails and fine, slightly curved bills. Their plumage is sexually dimorphic: males are glossy blue-black or olive above, yellow or white below, while females are duller. They inhabit montane and submontane forests, where they feed primarily on small fruits and berries.

children.name: Melanocharis nigra
children.description: The black berrypecker (Melanocharis nigra) is a species of bird in the family Melanocharitidae.

children.name: Melanocharis versteri
children.description:
The fan-tailed berrypecker (Melanocharis versteri) is a species of bird in the family Melanocharitidae. It is found in New Guinea. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.
The female is darker-colored and bigger than the male, an unusual feature for a passerine (Kikkawa 2003).

children.name: Melanocharis longicauda
children.description: The mid-mountain berrypecker or lemon-breasted berrypecker (Melanocharis longicauda) is a species of bird in the family Melanocharitidae. It is found in the New Guinea Highlands. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Melanocharis arfakiana
children.description: The obscure berrypecker (Melanocharis arfakiana) is a small passerine bird from the berrypecker family Melanocharitidae.

children.name: Melanocharis striativentris
children.description: The streaked berrypecker (Melanocharis striativentris) is a species of bird in the family Melanocharitidae.

children.name: Rhamphocharis nocturnalis
children.description: The Nocturnal Berrypecker is a nocturnal species that roosts in dense forest canopies, foraging primarily at night for small fruits and insects. Their feathers are adapted to reduce heat loss during the cool nights.

children.description: Melanocharis citreola (Satin berrypecker) is a berrypeckers species found in its native region.

children.description: Melanocharis crassirostris (Spotted Berrypecker) is a melanocharitidae species found in its native region.

children.description: Melanocharis chloroptera is a melanocharitidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Rhamphocharis
children.description: A small genus of berrypeckers with notably thick, deep bills adapted for crushing seeds and hard fruits, endemic to the mountain forests of New Guinea. They are medium-sized by melanocharitid standards, with spotted underparts that provide good camouflage in the forest gloom.

children.name: Rhamphocharis crassirostris
children.description: The thick-billed berrypecker (Melanocharis crassirostris) is a species of bird in the berrypecker and longbill family Melanocharitidae. It is found in New Guinea. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forest. The spotted berrypecker (Rhamphocharis piperata) was formerly considered conspecific (with both species being grouped under the common name "spotted berrypecker" but with the scientific name R. Crassirostris), but it was split as a distinct species by the IOC in 2021.

children.name: Rhamphocharis piperata
children.description: Rhamphocharis piperata (Spotted Berrypecker) is a berrypeckers species found in its native region.

children.name: Toxorhamphus
children.description: Small, long-billed berrypeckers found in New Guinea, closely related to the true berrypeckers. They have relatively long, slender bills adapted for feeding on nectar and small fruits, filling an ecological niche similar to sunbirds.

children.name: Toxorhamphus novaeguineae
children.description: The yellow-bellied longbill or green-crowned longbill (Toxorhamphus novaeguineae) is a species of bird in the family Melanocharitidae. It is found in New Guinea. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Toxorhamphus poliopterus
children.description: The slaty-headed longbill or grey-winged longbill (Toxorhamphus poliopterus) is a species of bird in the family Melanocharitidae. It is found in the New Guinea Highlands. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Oedistoma
children.description: Tiny, long-billed birds from New Guinea, among the smallest members of the berrypecker family. They have fine, decurved bills adapted for feeding on nectar and small insects, and were once considered part of the flowerpecker family.

children.name: Oedistoma iliolophus
children.description: The spectacled longbill (Oedistoma iliolophus), also known as dwarf longbill, plumed longbill or dwarf honeyeater, is a species of bird in the family Melanocharitidae.

children.name: Oedistoma pygmaeum
children.description: The pygmy longbill or pygmy honeyeater (Oedistoma pygmaeum) is a species of bird in the family Melanocharitidae.

children.name: Oedistoma spectaculare
children.description: A tiny longbill with a distinctive white eye-ring (spectacles), olive-green upperparts, and yellowish underparts, found in the montane forests of New Guinea. It has a fine decurved bill used for feeding on nectar and small insects. It is an active, acrobatic forager, often hovering at flowers.
